claims: A mortgage is a secured loan used to purchase or refinance real estate.
Lenders can take ownership of the property through foreclosure if mortgage repayments fail.
Mortgage requirements include a credit check, income verification, and a down payment.
Most borrowers choose 15-year or 30-year mortgage terms.
Mortgage rates range from 5.74% to 6.37% as of early April 2026.
The property serves as collateral for a mortgage loan.
Mortgage loans are repaid with interest over a set term.
Monthly mortgage payments usually include principal, interest, taxes, and homeowners insurance (PITI).
Monthly mortgage payments include private mortgage insurance (PMI) if the down payment is less than 20%.
Fixed-rate mortgages have interest rates that remain the same for the life of the loan.
Adjustable-rate mortgages (ARM) have rates that can change periodically.
Conventional mortgages are not insured by the federal government.
FHA, VA, and USDA loans are government-backed loans.
FHA, VA, and USDA loans often require lower down payments.
Lenders require a credit score for mortgage applications.
Lenders require proof of income and employment for mortgage applications.
Lenders require a debt-to-income (DTI) ratio for mortgage applications.
A 20% down payment avoids private mortgage insurance (PMI).
